To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the developmental component of cancer gene expression is a universal phenomenon and that the developmental gene expression of cancer is not a random phenomenon.

cancer and development are transcriptionally related, that this relationship can be quantified, that it is a universal feature, that it is not a one-size-fits-all phenomenon but is tissue specific and that the developmental component of cancer is not random, but follows distinct biological leit-motifs.

(a) cancer gene expression is strongly influenced by the developmental background of the tissue of origin, (b) the imprint of development is a universal feature that is shared across different tumor types and developmental time courses, (c) the imprint of developmental expression in cancers is not uniform, (d) the developmental imprint in cancers is not limited to a single developmental stage but extends over a large part of the developmental time course, (e) the imprint of the developmental transcriptome in tumors is not limited
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the developmental component of cancer and provides a comprehensive overview of the relationship of the neoplastic transcriptome to developmental gene expression.
the question of whether cancer gene expression can be interpreted in the light of development.
a global analysis of cancer gene expression in a biological context and it demonstrates that cancer gene expression is a reflection of developmental gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cancer is not a developmental process but that it is a disease of development.
cancer and development have more in common than we thought.
cancer is not development, but it has a developmental component.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene expression signatures in cancer and development are not merely a reflection of a common cellular state but are a reflection of the developmental origin of the tissue of origin.
the cancer transcriptome is a developmental transcriptome, but that it is not the developmental transcriptome.
the developmental component of human cancers is a universal phenomenon and that the developmental signature of a cancer is largely determined by its tissue of origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmental imprint on cancer is not a universal phenomenon but that there are significant differences between tumor types with respect to this aspect of their gene expression.
cancer is a developmental disease, but not in the same way in every cancer type.

the developmental imprint of human cancers is a general phenomenon and that it is not limited to the expression of a small set of master regulators but rather encompasses the expression of a large number of genes.
